title: English 7
summary: English textbook for grade 7 of Kyrgyz- and Russian-medium schools (А. Юсупова, Н. Мараш-Оглы, А. Шакирова, Ж. Набиев; Bishkek, «Билим-компьютер», 2012; Kyrgyz title «Англис тили», Russian «Английский язык»). Part I has four units of four lessons each: I and the world I live in; a good book is a good friend; eat to live, not live to eat; sports, health and hobby. Part II is supplementary material and a reference grammar, Part III an appendix, Part IV a reader, the syllabus and an English–Kyrgyz–Russian vocabulary. Grammar explanations and glosses are given in Kyrgyz and Russian.

sections.chapterTitle: I And The World I Live In
sections.title: Summer holidays
sections.summary: The lesson opens Unit I «I And The World I Live In». Pupils practise the sound [a:] with the poem «The telephone» by Alfred H. Miles, talk about how they spent their summer holidays and learn the use of the indefinite article a, an and the definite article the. The reading text «My summer holidays» tells how a pupil spends June at the seaside, July at a camp near a forest and August in the country helping his grandparents. A joke, sentence-building tasks and an essay «My summer holidays» complete the lesson.
objectives: Practise the sound [a:] and learn the poem «The telephone» by heart
Speak about summer holidays and make up a dialogue «How I spent my summer holidays»
Learn the use of the indefinite article a, an and the definite article the
Read and discuss the text «My summer holidays» and write an essay on the topic

keyTerms.definition: There are two articles in Modern English: the indefinite article a, an and the definite article the. (Kyrgyz: белгилүү the, белгисиз a, an; Russian: неопределенный артикль – a, an и определенный артикль the.)
Белгисиз артикль; неопределенный артикль. In the plural form the indefinite article a is not used (a door – doors).
Белгилүү артикль; определенный артикль. Used in the singular and plural: the door – the doors, the mushroom – the mushrooms.
журналдар жана гезиттер; журналы и газеты

facts: There are two articles in Modern English: the indefinite article a, an and the definite article the.
In the plural form the indefinite article a is not used: a door – doors, but the door – the doors; a mushroom – mushrooms, the mushroom – the mushrooms.
Phonetics: the sound [a:] is practised with the poem «The telephone» by Alfred H. Miles («Friends a hundred miles apart / Sit and chatter heart to heart…»).

Text «My summer holidays»: the pupil spends June at the seaside; in July goes to a camp two hours from home near a forest, where children pick berries and mushrooms, swim, play games, read and dance; in August visits the grandparents in the country, waters the plants, takes care of pets and helps repair the old house.
Joke (ex. 9): Thomas's brother is crying because Thomas is eating his cake and won't give him any – and he cried while Thomas was eating his own cake, too.
Speaking pattern (ex. 11): «The sun is round and so is a ball.»
experiments: Speak about your summer holidays: Do you like summer? Where and how did you spend your summer holidays?
Pair-work. Choose a partner and make up a dialogue «How I spent my summer holidays».
Read and act out the joke about Thomas and his brother.
Chain game: practise saying «The sun is round and so is a ball», then think of other items to replace a ball.
Write an essay «My summer holidays».
questions: 1. Read and learn by heart. («The telephone» by Alfred H. Miles)
2. Speak about your summer holidays. – Do you like summer? – Where and how did you spend your summer holidays?
3. Pair-work. Choose a partner and make up a dialogue «How I spent my summer holidays».

4. Make up questions to the following sentences and ask your classmates. – Summer is a wonderful season for everyone. – People are fond of travelling in summer. – They enjoy the beauty of nature. – School children like to swim in summer.

5. Fill in the gaps with articles a, an, the, where it is necessary. … Mrs. Brown has … new car. There is … table, … telephone, … radio. … Mrs. Brown is sitting at … desk, she is speaking on … telephone now and her son is at … computer. … Mrs. Brown and her son are busy at … home today.

6. Fill in the gaps with a, an, some, where it is necessary. … tea, … eagle, … car, … house, … tomatoes, … salt, … eye, … aunt, … blouse, … farmers, … apple, … cup, … egg, … union, … plates, … pepper, … horse, … water, … money, … milk
7. Read and discuss the text. («My summer holidays»)

8. Answer the questions. a. What do you prefer to do during your summer holidays? b. You like to spend summer holidays in the country, don't you? c. Whom do you like to spend your summer holidays with? d. What do you usually pick up in the forest? e. Can you swim? f. What season do you like best of all?
9. Read and act out the joke.

10. Make up sentences from the following words. a. Not far/ I/ from/ the school/ live. b. Olga's/ is/ farmer/ father/ a good. c. Now/ her/ is/ in/ playing/ daughter/the yard. d. When/ usually/ you/ get up/ do/? e. John/ interesting/ give/ you/ an/ book/ can/.
11. Sunshine comes from the sun, which is round. What else can you think of that is round? Practice saying «The sun is round and so is a ball.» Then think of other items to replace a ball.
12. Write an essay «My summer holidays».

sections.chapterTitle: I And The World I Live In
sections.title: School life
sections.summary: The lesson is about school life. Pupils practise the sound [i:] with W. Blake's «A cradle song», speak on proverbs about thinking before speaking and learn what an adjective is. The text «My school» describes a large, light three-storey school with workshops, computer classes, a dining room, a library and school concerts; the passage «Schools in England» introduces the English system of education. Pupils complete a dialogue about their school, make negative sentences and act out school jokes.
objectives: Practise the sound [i:] and learn «A cradle song» by W. Blake by heart
Speak on the proverbs «Think today and speak tomorrow», «Think before you speak»
Learn the adjective as a part of speech and put questions to adjectives
Read and retell the text «My school»; discuss the system of education in England
Compare schools in Kyrgyzstan and in England

keyTerms.definition: The Adjective is a word expressing a quality of a substance. (Kyrgyz: Сын атоочтор нерсенин сын-сапатын билдирет жана «кандай?» деген суроого жооп берет. Russian: Имя прилагательное обозначает признак предмета, т. е. его качество или свойство, и отвечает на вопрос какой?)

facts: The Adjective is a word expressing a quality of a substance; it answers the question «what?/what kind?» (кандай? / какой?). Examples from the lesson: large, beautiful, big, interesting, unusual, good.

Proverbs: «Think today and speak tomorrow» (Бүгүн ойлоп, эртең сүйлө / Сегодня подумай, а завтра скажи); «Think before you speak» (Айтылган сөз – атылган ок, экөө бирдей кайрылбайт / Слово не воробей, вылетит – не поймаешь).

Text «My school»: the school is large and light, has three floors, a big workshop on the ground floor, a wood work room for boys, a manual work room for girls on the third floor, computer classes, a dining room and a library without a reading-room; pupils study Kyrgyz, Russian, English, Literature, Maths, History, Biology, Geography, Music and organize concerts and parties.

Schools in England: there are infant schools, junior schools and secondary schools. British children begin school at five, study at junior schools for four years, then take examinations and go to a secondary school from eleven till sixteen; they don't go to school on Saturdays and Sundays.
Kinds of schools in England: grammar, modern, comprehensive, private and public schools.
Phonetics: the sound [i:] is practised with «A cradle song» by W. Blake («Sleep, sleep, beauty bright…»).
experiments: Speak on the proverbs «Think today and speak tomorrow» and «Think before you speak».
Listen to the passage «Schools in England» and discuss it; compare our schools and English schools.
Pair-work. Complete and act out the dialogue between Bolot and Sasha about their schools.
Read and act out the jokes about writing in the dark and Tommy's mother the teacher (role play).
questions: 1. Read and learn by heart. («A cradle song» by W. Blake)
2. Speak on the proverbs. Think today and speak tomorrow. Think before you speak.

3. Put questions to the underlined words. a. Our school is large and light. b. There are many beautiful flowers and trees. c. There is a big school library. d. We study many interesting subjects at school. e. We organize unusual concerts, parties when we celebrate our holidays. f. I go to school and get good knowledge.
4. Read and retell the text. («My school»)
5. Listen to the passage and discuss. («Schools in England»)
6. Find new words from the text «Schools in England», translate and make up sentences with them.

7. Pair-work. Complete and act out the dialogue. (Bolot and Sasha: What is the number of your school? Is your school big or small? How many floors does your school have? …) Do you like your school? How long does it take you to get to your school? What kind of schools are there in England? Do English boys and girls go to school on Saturdays and Sundays? Can you compare our schools and English schools?

8. Make up negative forms of the sentences. a. She goes to the private school. b. I am playing football for our school team. c. We live near the mountains. d. My father works in the office from 9 a.m. till 6 p.m. e. He will spend weekends with his friends.
9. Read and act out the jokes.

sections.chapterTitle: I And The World I Live In
sections.title: Family life
sections.summary: The lesson is about family life. Pupils practise the sound [ɔ] with A. H. Miles's poem «Balls», learn the degrees of comparison of adjectives and read the texts «About myself» (Ulan Batyrov from Talas) and «My family» (Cholpon describes her mother, father and sister). They translate sentences, tell about Rinat's day from pictures, play the game «An Interpreter», read Aaly Tokombayev's poem «The Ninth of May» and write an essay «My family».
objectives: Practise the sound [ɔ] and learn the poem «Balls» by heart
Learn the degrees of comparison of adjectives (comparative and superlative)
Listen to and retell the text «About myself»; describe people's appearance using adjectives
Speak about one's family and daily routine; write an essay «My family»

keyTerms.term: Degrees of comparison of adjectives / Сын атоочтун салыштырма даражалары / Степени сравнения прилагательных
keyTerms.definition: Adjective (сын атооч / прилагательное) – Comparative (салыштырма даража / сравнительная степень) – Superlative (күчөтмө даража / превосходная степень): large – larger – the largest; big – bigger – the biggest; old – older – the oldest.
Салыштырма даража; сравнительная степень: formed with -er (larger, bigger, older).
Күчөтмө даража; превосходная степень: formed with the … -est (the largest, the biggest, the oldest).
эң укмуштуу, сонун, татынакай; очаровательный, обаятельный

facts: Degrees of comparison: large – larger – the largest; big – bigger – the biggest; old – older – the oldest.
Text «About myself»: Ulan Batyrov is 13, lives in Talas, likes books and computer games, collects stamps, plays football; he is tall with black hair and grey eyes.

Text «My family»: Cholpon's family has four members – mother Saltanat Isanovna (40, a skilled doctor, tall and thin, brown eyes, turned-up nose), father Damir Nuruevich (42, a worker, round face, grey eyes), sister Venera (15, in the 10th form, plays the piano) and Cholpon (13, 7th form, fond of music and dancing).
Rinat's day (pictures): gets up early in the morning, salutes parents, goes to school, takes meals in time, brushes up the teeth, bathes daily, takes part in games, does his homework regularly.
Game «An Interpreter»: work in groups of three – a pupil from Kyrgyzstan (Russia), a pupil from England (America) and an interpreter who knows English and Kyrgyz (Russian).
«The Ninth of May» by Aaly Tokombayev (translated by Alex Miller) celebrates an eternal, unfading spring whose joyful song is carried from the mountains to the sea.
Phonetics: the sound [ɔ] is practised with the poem «Balls» by Alfred H. Miles.
Proverb: «Few words, many deeds».
experiments: Tell about Rinat's day using the pictures.
Write a topic about your working day.
Play a game called «An Interpreter» in groups of three.
Make up situations on the proverb «Few words, many deeds»; read the poem «The Ninth of May» and explain its meaning.
Read and act out the jokes about Johnny who is late and Esen writing a letter (role play).
Write an essay «My family».
questions: 1. Read and learn by heart. («Balls» by Alfred H. Miles)

2. Use the correct comparison forms of adjectives. a. My old house is large, but my new house is …. b. Linda's car was fast, but her new car is …. c. Mrs Black's hat is fancy, but her new hat is … . d. My uncle is energetic, but my cousin is … . e. Henry is thin, but his friend is … in the group. f. Tom's dictation was good. But mine was … in the class.

3. Use the correct comparison forms of adjectives. a. Steve is polite, he is … boy I know. b. Bill's coat is warm, but my coat is … . c. Jeff's old records were noisy, but his new ones are …. d. Rita's cat was hungry, but now it is … . e. My stove is (good) … than yours. f. The doctor's garden is (beautiful)… than yours.
4. Listen and retell the text. («About myself»)

5. Translate these sentences into English. a. Мен Баткенде жашаймын. / Я живу в Баткене. b. Мен китеп окуганды абдан жактырам. / Я очень люблю читать книги. c. Менин чачым кара жана узун. / У меня волосы черные и длинные. d. Мен дарыгер болгум келет. / Я мечтаю стать врачом. e. Менин үй-бүлөм чоң жана ынтымактуу. / Моя семья большая и дружная.
6. Tell about Rinat's day.
7. Write a topic about your working day.
8. Read and discuss the text using adjectives. («My family»)

9. Answer the following questions. a. Is your family large? b. What is your mother's name? c. How old is she? d. What is she? e. What is your father's name? f. How old is he? g. Do you have a sister or a brother? h. What are you? i. How old are you? j. What form are you in? k. What do the members of your family like to do in the evening?
10. Play a game called «An Interpeter».
11. a. Make up situations on the following proverb. «Few words, many deeds». b. Read the poem and explain its meaning. («The Ninth of May» by Aaly Tokombayev)
12. Read and act out the jokes.
13. Write an essay «My family».

sections.chapterTitle: I And The World I Live In
sections.title: Our duties
sections.summary: The lesson is about duties at home and at school. Pupils practise the sound [ŋ] with E. Gould's «The Washing-up Song», do dictionary work, listen to the text «Our duties in the house» and read «Our school duties», which lists what pupils and the pupil on duty must and should do. They practise prepositions of movement, revise verb tenses by choosing the correct item, solve riddles, read the joke «A clever mathematician», write an essay «My home and school duties» and act the play «Cinderella».
objectives: Practise the sound [ŋ] and learn «The Washing-up Song» by heart
Speak about household and school duties
Use prepositions of movement (past, under, up, down, into)
Revise verb tenses by choosing the correct verb form
Read and act the fairy-tale play «Cinderella»

keyTerms.definition: баланы чокундуруп ат коюучу эне; крестная мать
Dictionary work: find out the meaning and pronunciation of these words.

facts: Text «Our duties in the house»: the family of four helps Mum, a teacher; Dad goes shopping and cleans the carpets; the pupil tidies the room, washes up, sweeps the floor and sometimes makes tea or coffee; Mum cooks dinner and lays the table.

Text «Our school duties»: pupils must study well, be ready for lessons, come in time, listen to teachers, answer questions, do exercises, read, translate and retell texts, recite poems and describe pictures.
Pupils should not miss lessons or be late, talk or make a noise at the lessons, run or fight in the corridors, shout or be rude.

A pupil on duty should come before lessons, open the windows, wet the dusters, clean the blackboard, get chalk; after lessons water the flowers, dust chairs, tables, desks, shelves and sweep or clean the floor.
Prepositions of movement (ex. 5 key): go past, under, up, down, past, into (the hotel, the church, the hill, the bridge, the street, the stairs).
Joke «A clever mathematician»: a boy shares three oranges – one for Father, one for Mother, one for himself – and then eats his mother's one.

Play «Cinderella»: with the Fairy Godmother's help Cinderella goes to the King's ball in a white dress and glass slippers, dances with the Prince, runs away at twelve o'clock losing a slipper; the Heralds find that the slipper fits only Cinderella, and the stepsisters beg her pardon.
Phonetics: the sound [ŋ] is practised with «The Washing-up Song» by E. Gould.
experiments: Role-play. Act out «Our duties in the house».
Speak about your school duties.
Solve the riddles about the kettle and the fridge («Lives old Jack Frost»).
Read the joke «A clever mathematician» and explain it.
Write an essay «My home and school duties».
Group-work. Read and act the play «Cinderella».
questions: 1. Read and learn by heart. («The Washing-up Song» by E. Gould)
2. Dictionary work. Find out the meaning and pronunciation of the following words. feel, tidy, sweep, help
3. Listen to the text. («Our duties in the house»)
4. Role-play. Act out «Our duties in the house».
5. Put the right prepositions and match the sentences with pictures. a. Go … the hotel. b. Go … the church. c. Go … the hill. d. Go … the bridge. e. Go … the street. f. Go … the stairs.

6. Solve these riddles. a. On the cooker I'm puffing and puffing. Why are they torturing me for nothing? My lid is tinkling. Do make some tea! Switch off the cooker, and set me free. b. In our kitchen, all the year round, Lives old Jack Frost, all safe and sound.
7. Read and translate the text. («Our school duties»)
8. Speak about your school duties.

9. Choose the correct item. a. What are you cooking? It … very nice! (is smelling; smells; smelt) b. John … very hard at the moment. (worked; has worked; is working) c. … I help you to carry those bags? Yes, please. (shall; will; do) d. I … a new bike last week. (bought; have bought; will buy) e. They … in England for twenty years. (are living; live; have lived) … j. She … her ticket already. (is buying; bought; has bought)
10. Read the joke and explain it. («A clever mathematician»)
11. Write an essay «My home and school duties».
12. Group-work. Read and act the play. («Cinderella»)

sections.chapterTitle: A Good Book Is A Good Friend
sections.title: Books in our life
sections.summary: The lesson opens Unit II «A Good Book Is A Good Friend». Pupils practise the sound [u] with Ida W. Benham's «The listening woods», talk about books and learn personal pronouns. The text «Books are our friends» describes what children like to read and names «Alice in Wonderland» by Lewis Carrol as a favourite book; the text «Books in our life» explains the role of books, hand-written books in ancient times and printing. Pupils complete a dialogue about O'Henry's «The last leaf», work on the proverb «Choose a book as you choose a friend» and complete a cluster about kinds of books.
objectives: Practise the sound [u] and learn «The listening woods» by heart
Learn personal pronouns and choose correct possessive and demonstrative forms
Listen to, discuss and retell the text «Books are our friends»
Speak on the topic «Books in our life» and answer questions in writing

keyTerms.definition: The pronoun is a part of speech which points out objects and their qualities without naming them. (Kyrgyz: Ат атоочтор нерселерди атабай, бирок аларды билдирген сөздөр. Russian: Местоимения не имеют конкретного значения, но довольно часто заменяют собой существительные и прилагательные.)
I – я; you – вы, ты (ед. ч.); he – он; she – она; it – он, она, оно; we – мы; you – вы (мн. ч.); they – они.

facts: The pronoun is a part of speech which points out objects and their qualities without naming them.
Personal pronouns: I, you, he, she, it (singular); we, you, they (plural).

Text «Books are our friends»: children read stories, fairy-tales, poems and fables; little kids like big books with bright colours; schoolchildren prefer adventure books. Books teach us to be honest, kind, helpful and modest.
«Alice in Wonderland» by the English writer Lewis Carrol is a story about a girl and her adventures in a magic country, full of humour and funny episodes.

Text «Books in our life»: in ancient times books were written by hand; printing played an important role in the development of literature and culture; because it is difficult to buy all books, people use public libraries.
«The last leaf» by O'Henry is about great friendship; its main characters are Sue, Johnsy and Behrman.
Proverb: «Choose a book as you choose a friend».
Phonetics: the sound [u] is practised with «The listening woods» by Ida W. Benham.
experiments: Speak about books: Do you like reading books? Is it possible to live without books for you? What kind of books do you like to read?
Pair-work. Complete and act out the dialogue between Peter and Tolgonay about «The last leaf» by O'Henry.
Read, learn and make a situation on the proverb «Choose a book as you choose a friend».
Read and act out the joke and make up your own ones.
Complete the cluster «BOOKS»: fairy-tales, short-stories, novels …
questions: 1. Read and learn by heart. («The listening woods» by Ida W. Benham)

2. Speak about books. – Do you like reading books? – Is it possible to live without books for you? – Who read books for you when you were a child? – What kind of books do you like to read? – Books are our friends, aren't they?

3. Choose the correct pronoun. A: Excuse me, Mary. Are these socks (your/yours)? B: No, those are not (my/mine). (My/Mine) socks are red. A: I think that's (Jane/Jane's) new racket. B: No, that's not (her/hers). …
4. Circle the correct pronoun. A: Good afternoon. Can I help you? B: Yes. How much is (this/these) watch? A: It's $205. B: Oh. How much is (that/those) one? A: (It's/They're) $150. …
5. Listen and discuss the text. («Books are our friends»)
6. Retell the text «Books are our friends».
7. Pair-work. Complete and act out the dialogue. (Peter and Tolgonay about «The last leaf» by O'Henry)
8. Read, learn and make a situation on the proverb. «Choose a book as you choose a friend».
9. Read and speak on the topic. («Books in our life»)

10. Write answers to the following questions. a. What do you think, can books be our friends? Prove it. b. You like to read books, don't you? c. Do you have many books at home? d. Where can you buy books? e. Can you buy all books which you want to read? f. What is your favourite book?
11. Read and act out the joke and make up your own ones.
12. Make up 10 questions to the following sentence. Sue and Johnsy were poor artists who lived in a little New York district west of Washington Square.
13. Complete the cluster. (BOOKS: Fairy-tales, Short-stories, Novels …)

sections.chapterTitle: A Good Book Is A Good Friend
sections.title: At the library
sections.summary: The lesson is about libraries. Pupils practise the sound [ʌ] with A. Tennyson's «The brook», answer questions about libraries and learn the Present Indefinite Tense (affirmative, interrogative and negative forms with do/does). The text «At the library» describes school and public libraries, reading-rooms and the British Museum Library. Pupils practise questions, negatives and the verb to be (am, is, are), act out a joke and discuss what is better – reading a book or watching TV.
objectives: Practise the sound [ʌ] and learn «The brook» by heart
Learn the Present Indefinite Tense: affirmative, interrogative and negative forms
Use do/does and am, is, are correctly; make negative and Yes/No questions
Read and retell the text «At the library»
Discuss the good and bad points of television and books

keyTerms.term: The Present Indefinite Tense / Белгисиз Учур Чак / Настоящее Неопределенное Время
keyTerms.definition: I read – Do I read? – I do not read; He reads – Does he read? – He does not read; She reads – Does she read? – She does not read; We read – Do we read? – We do not read; You read – Do you read? – You do not read; They read – Do they read? – They do not read.
Auxiliary verbs of the Present Indefinite in questions and negatives; does is used with he, she, it.
Forms of the verb to be in the present: «Michael is from America.» Negative: «She is not at the library.» Question: «Is she at The British Museum Library?»

facts: Present Indefinite: in the 3rd person singular the verb takes -s (He reads, She reads); questions and negatives are made with do/does (Does he read? He does not read).
Text «At the library»: at the library you can find novels, poems, plays, books on history, geography and arts; adventure books are very popular; there is a reading-room with many tables and chairs.
A school library is a collection of textbooks and books for reading; the librarian helps the pupils to find books they need; teachers prepare for lessons there.
There are many public libraries in Bishkek and Moscow; one can take some books for two or three weeks. One of the biggest libraries in England is The British Museum Library.
Good points of TV: it keeps you informed about the rest of the world; bad points: it stops people talking. Good points of books: they give you much knowledge; bad points: it takes time.
Phonetics: the sound [ʌ] is practised with «The brook» by A. Tennyson.
experiments: Pair-work. Read, translate and act out the joke about ten hours over an English book.
Pair-work. Talk together and decide: What is better – reading a book or watching TV?
Discussion. How important is television to you? Answer these questions honestly.
Group work. What are the good points and bad points about television/books? Draw columns on a separate piece of paper and add to the list.
questions: 1. Read and learn by heart. («The brook» by A. Tennyson)
2. Think and answer the questions. a. Do you like to go to the libraries? b. Why do we need libraries? c. Do you have a library at school? d. Do you have any libraries in your city/town/village?

3. Insert do or does. a. … you swim well? Yes, I…. b. … your brother drive the car? Yes, he …. c. What … your teachers teach you? d. … Mr. Brown speak Russian? No, he … not. e. Where … you take books from? f. Alina … not drive a car. g. Aman … not like getting up early. h. How long … it take you to get to school? i. … she play chess well? No, she … not. j. What languages … Sergei speak?
4. Read and retell the text. («At the library»)

5. Answer the questions in writing. a. Do you have a library at home? b. What kind of books do you prefer to read? c. Do you have a library at school? d. Do you like to read newspapers and magazines? e. You visit your school library, don't you? f. What public libraries do you usually visit? g. Are there any libraries in England? h. What is the biggest library in London?

6. Make questions to the sentences. a. Sagyn works on a farm. Where … ? b. Alice lives in New York. Does … ? c. Alan goes out with friends in the evening. When … ? d. Nurbek likes tea with lemon. What … ? e. Mustafa goes to his office by underground. How … ? f. Mary works at a bookshop. Where … ? g. Mr. Anderson lives in the country. Who … ? h. We have six lessons on Tuesday. When… ?

7. Use the correct form of the verb. a. We (to be) always ready for our lessons. b. My mother (to cook) very well. c. My granny (not to work). d. My father (not to be) at home now. He (to work) at his office. e. What you (to do) now? I (to learn) the poem. f. Tom usually (to get up) at seven o'clock. g. Where you (to live) now? h. You (to understand) your teacher? i. Where Ann (to be)? She (to sleep). j. Sometimes he (to watch) TV in the evening.

8. Complete the following sentences. Use am, is, are. Murat … in at the library. Jane and Arnold … in the reading-room. She … watching TV at home. I … a schoolboy from Jany-Aryk village. We … pupils of Salieva school. You … from Kyrgyzstan.
9. Pair-work. Read, translate and act out the joke.
10. Make the following sentences negative. a. I am from England. b. My name is Jildyz. c. We are in Naryn. d. You are from France. e. Your name is Rahat.
11. Change the following sentences into Yes/No questions: a. It is a plane. b. Lola is in the hospital. c. His first name is Bolot. d. Your surname is Akmatov. e. You are from Osh.
12. Pair-work. Talk together and decide. What is better – reading a book or watching TV?

13. Discussion. How important is television to you? Answer these questions honestly. a. How many hours a week do you usually watch TV? b. «Television is a chewing-gum for our eyes.» Do you sometimes watch TV because you have nothing better to do? c. Do you watch television selectively? What do you think which is better – reading books or watching TV?
14. Group work. What are the good points and bad points about television/books?

sections.chapterTitle: A Good Book Is A Good Friend
sections.title: The history of books
sections.summary: The lesson tells the history of books. Pupils practise the sound [ei] with O. Nash's «Spring rain», learn the Past Indefinite Tense (affirmative, interrogative and negative forms with did) and work with a KWL chart. The text «From the history of books» explains how people moved from pictures to alphabetic writing, papyrus, skins and Chinese paper, hand-written books by monks, printing in Germany in the 15th century and Ivan Fedorov's first Azbuka (ABC) in 1574. The lesson also includes the joke «Don't trouble yourself», synonyms and antonyms, a dialogue and Barbara Walker's poem «Book look».
objectives: Practise the sound [ei] and learn «Spring rain» by heart
Learn the Past Indefinite Tense and make sentences interrogative and negative
Work with a KWL chart about the History of Books
Read and summarize the text «From the history of books»
Learn the poem «Book look» by heart

keyTerms.term: The Past Indefinite / Белгисиз Өткөн Чак / Прошедшее Неопределенное Время
keyTerms.definition: I played (wrote) – Did I play (write)? – I did not play (write); He played (wrote) – Did he play (write)? – He did not play (write); … They played (wrote) – Did they play (write)? – They did not play (write).
Auxiliary verb of the Past Indefinite in questions and negatives: Did he play? He did not play.
Know – What do I already know about the topic? Want to know – What do I want to know about the topic? Learnt – What have I learnt about the topic?
падыша; монарх (as glossed in the book)
эсте тутуу, унутпоо, эсте сактоо; помнить
Жок, чын эле эч качан!; Нет, действительно никогда!
to leave = departure, parting ≠ stay; lucky = happy ≠ unhappy.

facts: Past Indefinite: regular verbs take -ed (played), irregular verbs have special forms (wrote); questions and negatives are formed with did + infinitive (Did he play? He did not play).
At first men learned to draw pictures, then letters and alphabetic writing appeared; for a long time people used papyrus and skins of different animals to write on; then the Chinese invented paper.
All books were written by hand with pen and ink, mostly by monks; it took many years to make one copy of a book, so books were very expensive and those who had twenty books were considered very rich.
Men learned how to print in Germany in the middle of the fifteenth century.

The man who invented the art of printing in Russia was Ivan Fedorov; he started his work in Moscow and in 1574 printed the first Azbuka (ABC), which helped people to learn the alphabet and taught them to read.
Joke «Don't trouble yourself»: a woman keeps forcing an old man back into his seat on a bus, though he only wants to get off – she has already carried him three blocks beyond his destination.
«Book look» by Barbara Walker: since books are friends they need much care; use book-marks, don't turn a book upon its face; books are meant to read, not to cut or colour.
Phonetics: the sound [ei] is practised with «Spring rain» by O. Nash.
experiments: Work with a KWL chart: list what you know, want to know and have learnt about the History of Books.
Read and act out the joke «Don't trouble yourself»; think what you would do in the place of the old man or the young lady.
Fill in the gaps in the dialogue about going to the library.
Learn the poem «Book look» by heart.
questions: 1. Read and learn by heart. («Spring rain» by O. Nash)
2. Make the sentences interrogative and negative. a. John woke up at a quarter to seven. b. She went to the library yesterday. c. He began work at nine sharp. d. He was in France last year.

3. Make the sentences interrogative and negative. a. He took his children to the Zoo. b. Mary was a good pupil. c. They saw a new film on Monday. d. They had breakfast before they went out. e. His wife cooked some scones for breakfast. f. The people of Pine Clearing were proud of their school. g. My mother bought some vegetables for supper. h. They had a lot of problems with their son.

4. Make questions to the sentences. a. He watered the plants in the garden on Monday. Who … ? Where … ? What… ? When … ? b. She got up at 10.00 a.m. on Sunday. Who … ? What time … ? When … ? Did…? c. We were in the cinema last week. Who … ? Where … ? When … ?

5. Work with KWL chart. a. List things you already know about the History of Books in the first column. b. List things you want to know about the History of Books in the second column. c. List things you have learnt about the History of Books in the third column.
6. Read the text and summarize it. («From the history of books»)

7. Match the sentences. (You can find / For a long time people / Most of this writings / Most people / Books were considered / Now we find it hard / In 1574 he printed – with: to be very rich, them in every house, to imagine the bookless, the first Azbuka (ABC), used papyrus and skins, were done by monks, had no books at all)

8. Listen and say true or false. a. It is practically impossible today to imagine our life without books. b. At first men learned to draw pictures. c. In 1587 Ivan Fedorov printed the first Azbuka (ABC). d. It took one year to make one copy of a book. e. Books are printed in great numbers. f. Books are not printed all over the world. g. It is possible to live without books.
9. Rhyming words. Match the words in column A with their rhymes in column B. A: wife, well, pine, pie, in, eleven, bed. B: chin, eye, head, life, seven, smell, vine.
10. Read and act out the joke. («Don't trouble yourself»)
11. Think and answer. a. What would you do in the place of an old man? b. What would you do if you were a young lady?
12. Give the synonyms of the words. (to leave, lucky, vacant seats, good-looking, trouble, carry, take care – synonyms and antonyms)
13. Fill in the gaps in the dialogue. A: Did you go to the library? B: … A: Why not? B: … A: Did Nick get the book from the library on Monday? B: … A: Couldn't he? Why not? B: … A: …
14. Learn the poem by heart. («Book look» by Barbara Walker)

sections.chapterTitle: A Good Book Is A Good Friend
sections.title: At the bookshop
sections.summary: The lesson is about visiting a bookshop. Pupils practise the sound [ai] with O. Nash's «The lion», learn the Future Indefinite Tense (shall/will) and write about Bolot's plans for next week. The text «Visiting the bookshop» tells how three friends prepare for the 1st of September, the Day of Knowledge, and buy an English book about English customs and traditions. Pupils act out short conversations about books, read about famous writers and their characters, practise verb forms and phrasal verbs, write an essay «My favourite writer» and act the play «Tom doesn't want to go to school» after Mark Twain.
objectives: Practise the sound [ai] and learn «The lion» by heart
Learn the Future Indefinite Tense with shall/will: affirmative, interrogative and negative forms
Read and translate the text «Visiting the bookshop»
Learn about famous Kyrgyz, Russian, English and American writers and their characters
Write an essay «My favourite writer» and act the play after «The Adventures of Tom Sawyer»

keyTerms.term: The Future Indefinite / Белгисиз Келээр Чак / Будущее Неопределенное Время
keyTerms.definition: I shall (will) go. – Shall I go? – I shall not go. He will go. – Will he go? – He will not go. She will go. We shall go. – Shall we go? – We shall not go. You will go. They will go. – Will they go? – They will not go.
Auxiliary verbs of the Future Indefinite: shall with I and we, will with he, she, you, they.
бир нерсе үчүн акча төлөө; платить за что-либо
A writer is a man or a woman (a person) who writes books. They are authors.
менин тишим кыймылдап жатат; У меня шатается зуб.

facts: Future Indefinite: shall/will + infinitive (I shall go, He will go); questions put shall/will first (Will he go?); negatives add not (He will not go).
The 1st of September is a very popular holiday among pupils – the Day of Knowledge.

Text «Visiting the bookshop»: Dima and Erbol invite the narrator to visit bookshops on the 25th of August; they go to the bookshop in Masaliev street to buy copy-books, pens and pencils and buy an English book about Easter, April Fool's Day, Christmas Day and Boxing Day in England.

Famous writers in Kyrgyzstan: Aitmatov, Omurkulov, Mavlyanov; in Russia: Chukovsky, Marshak, Pushkin, Tolstoi; English writers: Defoe, Swift, Dickens, Kipling; American writers: Twain, London, Hemingway.

Favourite heroes: Jamilya and Daniyar (Ch. Aitmatov), Tatiana and Evgeniy (A. S. Pushkin), Robinson Crusoe (Daniel Defoe), Tom Sawyer (Mark Twain), Oliver Twist (Charles Dickens), Mowgli (Rudyard Kipling), Mary Poppins (Pamela Travers). They are kind, brave, quick, witty and honest.
Children read fairy-tales about Aladdin, the Sleeping Beauty, the Swan Princess, Cinderella.

Play «Tom doesn't want to go to school» (after The Adventures of Tom Sawyer by Mark Twain): Tom pretends to be dying to stay at home; Aunt Polly sees his loose tooth, pulls it out with a thread and sends him to school.
Phonetics: the sound [ai] is practised with «The lion» by O. Nash.
experiments: Write what Bolot's plans are for next week, then write about your plans.
Listen, read and act the «Short conversations» about books (Mark Twain, «Brown Wolf» by Jack London, books for children).
Read and say what you have learnt about famous writers.
Write an essay «My favourite writer».
Group work. Read and act the play «Tom doesn't want to go to school».
questions: 1. Repeat after the teacher and learn by heart. («The lion» by O. Nash)

2. Write what Bolot's plans are for next week. Then write about your plans. (Monday – tidy the room, Tuesday – repair a car, Wednesday – meet his friend, Thursday – fly to London, Friday – go sightseeing, Saturday – eat out with friends, Sunday – return back home)

3. Think and answer the questions. a. Are you fond of reading? b. Where do you usually get books? c. Do you like to buy books? d. Where can you buy books? e. How often do you go to the bookshops? f. What can you buy in the bookshops? g. Is there a bookshop near your house?
4. Read and translate the text. («Visiting the bookshop»)

5. Choose the correct item. a. I … (likes, like) to read books. b. Helen … (does, do) her shopping. c. They … (go, went) to the library yesterday. d. Bill … (is writing, wrote) an exercise in his note-book now. e. My parents … (am, are) watching TV. f. Kanat … (buys. buy) a magazine in a bookshop. g. Books … (are, is) our friends. h. Books … (teach, write) us to be honest, kind, helpful and modest.
6. Listen, read and act. («Short conversations»)
7. Read and say what you have learnt about famous writers. («Writers and the characters of their books»)
8. Complete the sentences. a. A writer is … b. There are many famous writers … c. The main and favourite heroes are … d. All children like … e. Little children listen to …
9. Put 10 questions to these sentences. a. The 1st of September is the Day of Knowledge. b. Little children listen to their favourite tales before they go to bed.
10. Give three forms of the following verbs. leave, buy, enjoy, write, give, listen, cook, speak, go, think.

11. Fill in up, down, on, off, away, round, back or out? a. Put … your hat. It's cold today. b. I don't feel well. I'm going to lie … for a minute. c. I fell … the stairs and broke my leg. d. The children stood … when the teacher arrived. e. Don't throw … that bottle. We can use it again. f. I would take … my jacket if I felt hot. g. I must remember to take the book … to the library. h. I'm going to take the dog … for a walk. i. I heard someone running behind me. I turned … and saw a girl in a track suit.
12. Write an essay «My favourite writer».
13. Group work. Read and act the play. («Tom doesn't want to go to school», after The Adventures of Tom Sawyer by Mark Twain)

sections.chapterTitle: Eat To Live, Not Live To Eat
sections.title: Food and meals
sections.summary: The first lesson of Unit III «Eat To Live, Not Live To Eat» introduces the topic of food and meals. Pupils learn the poem «Butterfly» for the sound [b], talk about their meals and favourite food, revise the Present Continuous Tense and read the texts «Meals» and «English Meals» about the four meals of the day and traditional English food.
objectives: Speak about meals and favourite food
Revise the Present Continuous Tense and contrast it with the Present Simple
Read and retell the texts «Meals» and «English Meals»
Learn new words connected with food and meals

keyTerms.term: The Present Continuous Tense (Узак Учур Чак / Настоящее Длительное Время)
keyTerms.definition: I am speaking. He is speaking. Am I speaking? I am not speaking. — formed with am/is/are + verb-ing
бир аз тамактанып алуу; перекусить на ходу
the meals of the day described in the text «Meals»

facts: Proverb: «Eat to live, not live to eat».
Text «Meals»: people usually have four meals a day — breakfast, lunch, dinner and supper; a snack is a light meal between them.
Text «English Meals»: a traditional English breakfast is big — sausages, bacon, eggs, tomatoes and mushrooms; nowadays many people have cereal.
The British eat marmalade made from oranges; jam is made from other fruit.
«Tea» in Britain is both a drink and a meal; afternoon tea and cream teas with scones are traditional.
The evening meal is the main meal of the day, usually between 6 and 8 o'clock; on Sunday many families have a traditional lunch of roast meat.
The British also like Italian, French, Chinese and Indian food and take-away meals, so eating in Britain is quite international.
experiments: Speak about meals: how many meals you have a day, your favourite food, and explain the proverb «Eat to live, not live to eat».
Make your own word search with words connected with food and give it to your partner.
Work in pairs: act out the dialogue and role-play a situation in the park at lunchtime.

2. Speak about meals. a. How many meals do you have a day? b. What is your favourite food? c. When do you have it? d. Explain the proverb «Eat to live, not live to eat».
3. Look at the list of food and drink. What do you like? What don't you like?

sections.title: American meals
sections.summary: The lesson «American meals» practises the Past Continuous Tense and vocabulary for food. Pupils learn the poem «Aunts» by V. Graham for the sound [tʃ], read a jumbled text about American meals, make shopping lists, sing «Peas Pudding Hot» and compare Kyrgyz and Russian national dishes.
objectives: Learn and use the Past Continuous Tense
Read and arrange a jumbled text about American meals
Name food, drinks, fruit and vegetables
Compare Kyrgyz and Russian meals

keyTerms.term: The Past Continuous Tense (Узак Өткөн Чак / Прошедшее Длительное Время)
keyTerms.definition: I was swimming. You were swimming. Was I swimming? I was not swimming. — formed with was/were + verb-ing
Kyrgyz national food and drink; kymyz is made of horse milk

facts: Text «American Meals»: Americans usually eat breakfast — eggs, toast with jelly, tea or coffee, sometimes pancakes.
Lunch is between 12 and 1 o'clock; the noon meal is light and quick — Americans often «eat and run».
Dinner, at about 5 or 6 pm, is the largest meal of the day: meat (chicken, turkey, beef, pork), potatoes, vegetables such as carrots, peas, beets, tomatoes and green beans, salad and milk.
Proverb: «Appetite comes with eating».
Past Continuous is used with Past Simple for an action interrupted by another: John was listening to the radio when ...

Pair-work: make a shopping list and act out a dialogue between a shop assistant and a customer.
Group work: make a Venn diagram of similarities and differences between Kyrgyz and Russian meals.

Listen and sing «Peas Pudding Hot».

sections.chapterTitle: Eat To Live, Not Live To Eat
sections.title: I'm a good cooker
sections.summary: The lesson «I'm a good cooker» deals with cooking and table manners. Pupils learn the Present Perfect Tense, the poem «Algy met a bear» by E. Lear for the sound [dʒ], learn how to lay the table, act out café dialogues, write a pizza recipe and acrostic poems, practise plural nouns and It is / There is, and read the poem «This Is Just to Say» by William Carlos Williams.
objectives: Learn and use the Present Perfect Tense with just, already, yet, for, so far, ago
Describe how to lay the table
Read and write a recipe
Form plurals of nouns and use It is / There is

keyTerms.term: The Present Perfect Tense (Учурга чейинки Бүткөн Чак / Настоящее Совершенное Время)
keyTerms.definition: I have worked. He has worked. Have I worked? I have not worked. — formed with have/has + Participle II
Acrostic poems are based on a word or name. The word may be the beginning of each line, or one of the letters in the word or phrase.
knife – knives, child – children, son-in-law – sons-in-law, passer-by – passers-by, woman – women, mouse – mice, gentleman – gentlemen, tooth – teeth

facts: A properly laid table has a soup spoon, a glass, a plate, a big knife and fork, a small plate for bread, a small knife and a spoon and fork for dessert.

Pizza recipe: 100 g flour, 25 g butter, a pinch of salt, 2 tomatoes, 50 g cheese, 50 g sausage; oil the pan, mix flour and salt, cut in the butter, add milk and mix into dough, put the dough into the pan, add the toppings and bake about 15 minutes in a hot oven.
Dialogues: I'm thirsty. — Would you like some tea?; ordering beefsteak, tomato juice, pizza and tea with lemon at a café.
«This Is Just to Say» by William Carlos Williams: the speaker apologises for eating the plums that were in the icebox.

Create your own pizza and give it a name.
Make up your own acrostic poems (FOOD, MEALS, APPLE).

sections.chapterTitle: Eat To Live, Not Live To Eat
sections.title: I like shopping
sections.summary: The lesson «I like shopping» is about buying food. Pupils learn the Past Perfect Tense, the poem «God made the bees» by L. Bowen for the sound [m], act out a dialogue at a food shop, learn measure words (a bottle of, a loaf of, a jar of ...), practise there is/are, to be, to have, do/does and prepositions of place, and act out the fairy-tale play «Three Bears».

Buy food in a shop using measure words
Use prepositions of place
Write an essay «Meals in Kyrgyzstan and England»

keyTerms.term: The Past Perfect Tense (Өткөн Учурга чейинки Бүткөн Чак / Прошедшее Совершенное Время)
keyTerms.definition: I had worked. Had I worked? I had not worked. — formed with had + Participle II
In combinations half simply means «partly» or «about 50%»: half dressed, half eaten, half empty, half full, half asleep.
a bottle of, a pound of, a loaf of, a box of, a bar of, a jar of, a bunch of, a dozen

facts: Dialogue «At a Food Shop»: Guzal buys two pounds of strawberries, a loaf of bread, a dozen eggs, a bottle of milk and a jar of honey.
There is / There are: There is a mouse ... There are bees ... Is there ...? Yes, there is.
Prepositions of place: in front of, under, on top of, behind, opposite, between, in, above, next to, on.
Play «Three Bears» (a fairy-tale): a little girl tastes the bears' milk — too hot, too cold, just right — hides under the table and runs away; the bears say «It is your fault, Father!».

Role-play at a market: say what you can and would like to buy and act out a dialogue.
Write an essay «Meals in Kyrgyzstan and England».
Group work: read and act the play «Three Bears».

2. Complete the sentences using Past Perfect.
3. Complete the sentences using Past Perfect.
4. Play the game «Say It Quickly».

10. The word half can be used with a number of other words. In these combinations, half simply means «partly» or «about 50%». Can you figure out what these phrases mean?

sections.chapterTitle: Sports, Health And Hobby
sections.title: Sport life
sections.summary: The first lesson of Unit IV «Sports, Health and Hobby» introduces sports. Pupils learn the poem «City» by L. Hughes, discuss proverbs about health and tastes, read the text «Sports in Our Life» about PT lessons, popular sports in Kyrgyzstan and national sports of Great Britain, learn names of sports equipment and read a text about tennis.
objectives: Speak about sports and favourite sports
Learn names of sports and sports equipment
Read and discuss the text «Sports in Our Life»
Group sports into indoor and outdoor

keyTerms.definition: skateboard, skates, trainers/sneakers, sports kit, swimming costume, tennis racket, helmet, roller-blades, hockey stick

facts: Proverbs: «Good health is above wealth» (Биринчи байлык – ден-соолук / Доброе здоровье дороже богатства); «There is no accounting for tastes» (О вкусах не спорят).
Text «Sports in Our Life»: pupils have PT lessons twice a week; sport helps to keep good health and not to catch cold.
Popular sports in our country include horse-racing, volleyball, gymnastics and ordo; athletics includes running and jumping.
National sports in Great Britain are cricket, football, rugby, table tennis, motorcar and boat racing.
Tennis can be played as singles, doubles or mixed doubles; it is a popular spectator sport.

Complete and tell the joke (optimist and pessimist) from memory.

sections.chapterTitle: Sports, Health And Hobby
sections.title: Sports and games
sections.summary: The lesson «Sports and games» teaches the Passive Voice (Present, Past, Future, Perfect and Continuous Passive) through sports texts. Pupils learn the poem «The Corn-Song» by J. G. Whittier, read texts describing sports, Aibek's diary and Jane Brown's letter about sports in England, write a letter about their own sport and interview a famous sportsperson.
objectives: Learn and use the Passive Voice
Name summer, winter, Olympic and non-Olympic sports
Read a letter about sports in England
Write a letter and interview questions about sport

keyTerms.term: The Passive Voice (Туюк Мамиле / Страдательный Залог)
keyTerms.definition: The Passive Voice is formed by means of the auxiliary verb to be in the required form and Participle II of the notional verb.
I am invited. I was invited.
I am being invited. I was being invited.

sections.chapterTitle: Part II
sections.title: Supplementary Material
sections.summary: Part II «Supplementary Material» opens with the Reference Grammar: the English alphabet with the names of the letters and a phonetics section on vowels, diphthongs and consonants.
facts: Part II contains the alphabet, phonetics (vowels, diphthongs, four ways of reading vowels, letter combinations, consonants), a table of irregular verbs and grammar notes in English, Kyrgyz and Russian.

sections.chapterTitle: Part II
sections.title: Reference Grammar
sections.summary: The Reference Grammar gives the English alphabet and phonetics, the four ways of reading vowels and letter combinations, a table of irregular verbs with Kyrgyz and Russian translations, and short rules with tables on the article, the adjective and its degrees of comparison, pronouns, the Indefinite, Continuous and Perfect tenses, the Passive Voice and the modal verbs. Rules are given in English, Kyrgyz and Russian.

keyTerms.definition: a: name, map, park, care; o: note, not, fork, more; e: be, bell, term, here; i: fine, sit, first, fire; u: tune, cup, turn, during
table of Infinitive (V1), Past (V2) and Participle II with Kyrgyz and Russian translations

The article is a structural part of speech used with nouns. There are two articles in Modern English: the indefinite article a, an and the definite article the. In the plural form the indefinite article a is not used.
The Adjective is a word expressing a quality of a substance.
long – longer – the longest; easy – easier – the easiest; big – bigger – the biggest. -er shows the difference between two things; -est shows the greatest degree.

The pronoun is a part of speech which points out objects and their qualities without naming them. Groups: personal, possessive, reflexive, reciprocal, demonstrative, interrogative, indefinite pronouns.

The Present Indefinite is formed from the infinitive without the particle to. In the third person singular the ending -s is added; after s, ss, ch, sh, tch, x, z and after the vowel o, -es is added. The interrogative and negative forms are formed with the auxiliary verb to do.
The Past Indefinite is formed by adding -ed or -d to the stem (regular verbs), or by changing the root vowel, or in some other ways (irregular verbs). Questions and negatives use did.
The Future Indefinite is formed by means of the auxiliary verbs shall and will and the infinitive without to. In Modern English there is the tendency to use will for all persons.
The Present Continuous is formed by means of the Present Indefinite of the auxiliary verb to be and Participle I of the notional verb.
The Past Continuous is formed by means of the Past Indefinite of the auxiliary verb to be and Participle I of the notional verb.
The Present Perfect is formed by means of the Present Indefinite of the auxiliary verb to have and Participle II of the notional verb.
The Past Perfect is formed by means of the Past Indefinite of the auxiliary verb to have and Participle II of the notional verb.

The Passive Voice is formed by means of the auxiliary verb to be in the required form and Participle II of the notional verb. The Future Continuous and the Perfect Continuous tenses are not found in the Passive Voice.

Modal verbs are used to show the speaker's attitude toward the action or state indicated by the infinitive: possible, impossible, probable, obligatory, necessary, advisable, etc. They are can (could), may (might), must (had to), should, ought, shall, will, would, need, dare; to be + Infinitive and to have + Infinitive also belong here.

facts: In the interrogative form the auxiliary verb is placed before the subject; in the negative form the particle not is placed after the auxiliary verb.
Every transitive verb in English can have the Active Voice and the Passive Voice.
Present, Past and Future Indefinite Passive: I am invited. I was invited. I shall be invited.
Modal verbs have no non-finite forms and therefore no complex verb forms.

sections.chapterTitle: Part III
sections.title: Appendix
sections.summary: Part III «Appendix» gives extra classroom material: «Twelve ways of winning people», the games «Create a New Sport» and «Create a New Holiday», matching tables of verb forms, the teacher activities «Umbrella» and «Picture the Past», tables of speech etiquette phrases in English, Kyrgyz and Russian, and riddles in verse.
facts: Twelve ways of winning people: begin in a friendly way; show respect for the other man's opinion; if you are wrong, admit it quickly; the only way to get the best of an argument is to avoid it; «A man convinced against his will is of the same opinion still».
Game «Create a New Sport»: choose an existing sport, change 3 rules, explain them, create a new name and draw an illustration.
Game «Create a New Holiday»: decide the date, who will celebrate it, what it honours, its traditions (food, clothing, music, decorations) and why people should celebrate it.
Matching: simple form and past tense, past form and past participle (write – wrote – written, speak – spoke – spoken).

«Umbrella» (Grammar: modals and Present Simple): pupils list advantages and disadvantages of a new tulip-like umbrella design; «Picture the Past» (Past Simple, Past Perfect, Future in the Past): pupils write sentences about a drawing of a past action.

Speech etiquette: Preference (Which do you prefer, ... or ...?), Invitation (Let me invite you to ...), Advice, Congratulations, Wishes, Playing Host (Make yourself at home), Disbelief (Really? You are joking), Ignorance (Sorry, I don't know; I have no idea).
Riddles «Pictures»: verse riddles about an abacus, a blackboard, a map, a TV set, a telephone, glasses, a light bulb, a book, a saw, a ruler, a pencil, a goose, an egg and others.

sections.chapterTitle: Part IV
sections.title: Reader
sections.summary: Part IV «Reader» contains twenty reading tasks with stories by English, American, Kyrgyz and Russian writers and documentary texts: funny stories about children and animals, extracts from «The Last Leaf», «Brown Wolf», «The Adventures of Tom Sawyer», «Robinson Crusoe» and «David Copperfield», a Kyrgyz story by Zhunai Mavlyanov, and texts about patriotism and space. Each text has a glossary in Kyrgyz and Russian and questions.
facts: Tasks 1–2. «The Last Leaf» (after O. Henry, 1862–1910): sick Johnsy believes she will die when the last ivy leaf falls; old painter Behrman paints a leaf on the wall, saves her and dies of pneumonia.
Task 3. «Mr. Tomata»: little Andy pretends to be Mr. Tomata and refuses to answer to his own name.
Tasks 4–5. «Brown Wolf» (after Jack London, 1876–1916): the dog Wolf, found by Walt Irvine and Madge, chooses to return to the North with his old master Skiff Miller.
Task 6. «The Andy Bird»: Andy pretends to be a bird in a tree and cannot get down; Daddy builds him a ladder.
Tasks 7–8. Mark Twain (1835–1910) and «The Adventures of Tom Sawyer»: Aunt Polly and the jam; Tom gets other boys to whitewash the fence for him.
Task 9. «The House with Stairs»: the dog Peter learns to go up and down stairs.
Task 10. Daniel Defoe (1660–1731) and «Robinson Crusoe»: shipwreck, the island, making a raft.
Task 11. «The Lucky Dog»: Phoebe the French poodle wants a dress and Grandmother knits her one.
Tasks 12, 14. Charles Dickens (1812–1870), «David Copperfield»: David runs away from his stepfather Mr. Murdstone and finds his aunt Miss Betsy Trotwood in Dover.
Task 13. «The Square Blue and White Animal»: Andy tries to fool Mother with an invented animal «Oh No».
Task 15. «Who Is Coming?»: Grandmother and Grandfather prepare for the visit of their four-year-old grandson Jefferson Jonas the third.
Task 16. Zhunai Mavlyanov (born 1923), «The Way Back Home»: old Usenkul mends the road unpaid while waiting for his sons Ernazar and Kulnazar to come back from the war.
Task 17. Sergei Mikhalkov (born 1913) and «They Loved Their Country»: fourteen-year-old Zhenya and his friends in Sevastopol die getting cartridges for the partisans.
Task 18. «49 Days Adrift in the Ocean»: in 1960 four Soviet soldiers (Ziganshin, Poplavsky, Kruchkovsky, Fedotov) drift on barge T-36 and are rescued by the U.S. Navy.
Tasks 19–20. «Exploring Space» (the solar system, satellites, Sputnik 1957, Yuri Gagarin on 12 April 1961) and cosmonaut Salijan Sharipov, born 1964 in Uzgen, Osh region.

Reader tasks: Unit 1 — Tasks 1–5, Unit 2 — Tasks 6–10, Unit 3 — Tasks 11–15, Unit 4 — Tasks 16–20.
8 hours are given to checking speaking and writing skills; the total is 105 hours.
